content.overview: Where the time for making an application to set aside the arbitral award under section 34 has expired, or such application having been made, it has been refused, the award shall be enforced in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in the same manner as if it were a decree of the Court. Filing of an application under section 34 does not by itself render the award unenforceable unless the Court grants a stay of operation of the award on a separate application under section 36(2)–(3).
content.glance: Award enforceable as a decree after s. 34 time expires or application is refused; s. 34 filing does not automatically stay enforcement unless Court grants stay.
content.study: Enforceability arises when the s. 34 period expires or a s. 34 application is refused. Enforcement is under the CPC as if the award were a decree. A s. 34 application does not automatically stay the award; stay requires a separate Court order under s. 36(2)–(3).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does filing a section 34 application automatically stay enforcement of the award?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Filing under section 34 does not by itself render the award unenforceable. Stay requires a separate application and a Court order under section 36(2)–(3).
